result.summary: Adds assert_true() and assert_false() helper functions to test_framework/util.py that enforce strict boolean comparison. Converts existing assert_equal(..., True) and assert_equal(..., False) invocations across more than 90 functional test files to the new helpers using a scripted diff.
result.problem: Boolean assertions in Python functional tests conventionally used assert_equal(expr, True/False), which is verbose and places the expected boolean literal at the end of long expressions, increasing cognitive load when reading tests.
evidence: PR description: 'The main point of this change is that assert_true()/assert_false() reduce cognitive tokens when scanning the code (equals to what...?)... assert_true([expression]) is different from plain assert [expression] in that assert is truthy while assert_true requires boolean True.'
result.scope_notes: Touches 94 files, but the bulk of the changes are mechanical and executed via scripted diff (sed), preceded by import fixups and an edge-case 3-argument assert_equal fix.
result.changed_since_previous: The commit history has been rebased and organized into preparatory cleanup commits (import fixups and an edge-case fix) followed by the scripted diff and unused-import removal.
result.card: This PR adds assert_true() and assert_false() helper functions to the functional test framework and migrates existing assert_equal calls comparing against boolean literals across the test suite via a scripted diff. It improves test code readability and ergonomics while ensuring strict boolean identity rather than truthiness. Importance is low because it is an internal test framework cleanup that alters neither node behavior nor test coverage.

risk.why: A typo or malformed transformation in the scripted diff could cause a functional test to fail or erroneously pass in CI.
